tagline: The key transit junction between the Bosphorus ferry system and the tram and funicular — not a destination in itself, but one of Istanbul's most important crossroads.

items.name: Kabataş İskelesi Çay Bahçesi
items.description: A tea garden by the ferry terminal with Bosphorus views. A pleasant 10-minute break between ferry and tram connections.

items.name: Kabataş Ferry Terminal
items.description: Ferries depart from here to the Princes' Islands, Üsküdar, Kadıköy, and Bosphorus villages. The view from the quayside is always excellent.

items.name: Dolmabahçe Palace
items.description: The lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace is a 5-minute walk north along the Bosphorus. One of Istanbul's most spectacular buildings.
items.tip: Book timed entry tickets online to avoid the queue. The Clock Tower and the Ceremonial Hall are the highlights.

tips: Kabataş is a major transit junction — tram T1, funicular F1 to Taksim, and Bosphorus ferries all connect here.
Not a neighbourhood to spend time in — use it as the transit point it was designed to be.
The walk north along the Bosphorus to Beşiktaş (15 min) or south to Fındıklı (10 min) is pleasant.
Dolmabahçe Palace is the main reason to exit here — combine the palace visit with onward transport.
